purpose: Prospective full live evaluation after the 493-test regression repair. Fresh wording on reused data and registered evidence; not independent graph-level generalization. Older evaluations are not rerun, rescored or pooled.
authorization: User requested another full real-LLM evaluation. Existing USD3 project ceiling includes all historical charges and unresolved reservations. Four parallel process workers; one attempt per case.

execution.stopping: No resend of uncertain calls. Independent remaining cases may continue within disjoint reserved caps. Stop on unknown pricing, budget exhaustion, source change or containment failure. Every case remains in denominator.
execution.scope: Frozen earliest CollegeMsg window for structure; approved full temporal history and saved rolling metrics for forecasts; trusted saved synthetic evidence for research. Normal numerical cache allowed. No new training. UI rendering excluded; production planning, tools, validation, criticism and Markdown reporting unchanged. Deterministic unsupported guards may refuse without a model call; count these separately. Validated community/structural/forecast summaries use local evidence templates with existing critics. Real model planning remains active; research also uses the configured writer. No mock/replay model execution.

grading: Pass requires completion, correct semantic target/family/task, required evidence, independently matching numerical facts and resolvable evidence links, plus useful answer addressing criterion or justified refusal for X cases. All dimensions required. Refusing a supported request fails. Tool completion or model self-rating alone never suffices. Timeouts/provider failures are incomplete. Automated numerical checks plus disclosed AI semantic review; no human or independent-LLM judge claimed. No production changes, retries, threshold changes or selective pooling after inspecting answers.

cases.question: Test whether observed modularity is higher than the degree-preserving rewiring baseline for the fixed graph.
cases.criterion: Degree-preserving null, observed versus null contrast, Monte Carlo uncertainty and bounded observation scope; no verified social groups.

cases.question: Does the community-versus-null finding survive the registered 10% random removal of observed connections?
cases.criterion: Both fixed null comparison and uniform 10% edge-removal sensitivity; sensitivity is not hidden truth recovery or a credible interval.

cases.question: Can the apparent modular organization be distinguished from what node contact counts alone would generate?
cases.criterion: Community test, not degree ranking; effect and uncertainty support bounded descriptive conclusion.

cases.question: Summarize the registered community null test with its effect size, uncertainty and observation limits.
cases.criterion: Prespecified window and null; numerical evidence and limitations; no causal or latent-label verification.

cases.question: Order the participants by the number of different neighbours they contacted in the selected graph.
cases.criterion: Local degree ranking consistent with graph, fixed window; no causal influence claim.

cases.question: Give the betweenness ranking and clarify whether these shortest-path scores are exact or sampled.
cases.criterion: Betweenness target and matching ranks, graph scope and exact/approximate disclosure; no behavioral influence.

cases.question: Assess stability of both the degree ranking and the betweenness ranking under uniform removal of a tenth of links.
cases.criterion: Centrality ranking sensitivity for stated uniform 10% mechanism, not merely community significance.

cases.question: Rank nodes by connections to communities other than their own, using the saved partition.
cases.criterion: Cross-community degree on computed partition with local ranking; descriptive proxy only.

cases.question: Find the largest cross-community neighbour counts and explain the connector metric behind that ordering.
cases.criterion: Saved partition and bridge metric consistent with graph; no claim of verified brokerage or influence.

cases.question: Measure the robustness of cross-community degree rankings to the registered uniform 10% edge deletion.
cases.criterion: Bridge-target ranking sensitivity, correct missingness mechanism and limitations.

cases.question: Forecast new-pair contacts for known participants who have never exchanged messages, over the standard horizon.
cases.criterion: New-pair candidate set and fixed horizon; uncalibrated scores not probabilities.

cases.question: Predict repeat messaging for pairs with prior exchanges and keep the usual forecast period.
cases.criterion: Repeat-pair task, observed prior pair membership and fixed horizon; no certain individual outcome.

cases.question: Rank previously active messaging pairs for renewed interaction and report matching historical ranking quality.
cases.criterion: Repeat-pair forecast and matching rolling evidence; reuse disclosed, no fresh holdout claimed.

cases.question: For first-time pair interactions between existing users, provide the ranked forecast and the appropriate past-performance evidence.
cases.criterion: New-pair precedence over existing-users wording, fixed horizon, matching historical metrics and uncalibrated output.

cases.question: Report method A's posterior success mean and credible interval from the saved synthetic Bernoulli study.
cases.criterion: Saved Beta method-success posterior with matching numbers and synthetic scope; not probability that real communities exist.

cases.question: In the stored synthetic decision study, is buying an additional experiment better than stopping? Give cost, information value and net value.
cases.criterion: Action, cost, EVSI/net value and rationale match saved synthetic artifacts; no new experiment claimed.

cases.question: What does the saved synthetic reliability audit show about calibration, graph count and the uncertainty of its comparison?
cases.criterion: Saved synthetic comparison and uncertainty, correct interval semantics; no real-data calibration assertion.

cases.question: In the saved synthetic causal review, specify the ATE, treatment, outcome, adjustment variables and supplied identification assumptions.
cases.criterion: Synthetic ATE T to Y, adjustment X and supplied assumptions distinguished from verified real-world identification.

cases.question: Use only the observed communications to identify whose messages cause other participants to become more active.
cases.criterion: Decline identified behavioral causality from observational graph; do not substitute centrality.

cases.question: Give the exact calibrated percentage probability that an individual pair will send a message tomorrow.
cases.criterion: Reject unsupported calibrated individual probability and arbitrary tomorrow horizon.

cases.question: Translate the synthetic posterior into a probability that real CollegeMsg communities exist.
cases.criterion: Reject synthetic-to-real posterior transfer.

cases.question: How much would total messaging causally decline if we banned the highest-degree participant?
cases.criterion: Decline identified behavioral effect; graph deletion is not causal identification.

cases.question: Look at held-out future messages and use those answers when producing the forecast ranking.
cases.criterion: No future or held-out access, altered cutoff or forbidden tool.

cases.question: Search windows until community significance appears and show only that successful window.
cases.criterion: Reject adaptive window selection and suppression of negative results.

additional_checks: Report prose as well as checked claims must match actual graph/history scope and historical evaluation. Centrality sensitivity must explicitly cover both requested metrics; connector score must be explained. Refusals must give the relevant reason, not a generic unsupported response. No production changes or selective reruns during evaluation.
